title: Async batch embedding client: jobs, polling, paged results
scenario: An asyncio client submits document batches as embedding jobs (bounded concurrency), retries 429/5xx creates with Retry-After or exponential backoff, polls jobs to completion, pages through results by token, and reports norms plus every failed batch.

verified.why_correct: Catching HTTPError and returning a Response looks like it hides errors, but it is deliberate: status handling happens in raise_for_status, and HTTPError (a URLError subclass) is the only exception that carries a status and body.
The header is in seconds and the body field in milliseconds, so only the body value is divided by 1000. `is not None` keeps a legitimate 0 ms.

bugs.title: Fresh semaphore per batch
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_concurrency_cap: '6 not less than or equal to 2'. All six batches hit the server at once. Every result is still correct.
bugs.why: Each batch acquires its own brand-new semaphore, so nothing is shared and every batch starts at once. The shared `sem` built above is never used.
hints: How many requests were in flight at the peak, and how many batches are there?
Look at what run_one acquires before starting a batch.
probes: Why does every result still come out right without the limit?
Why must the semaphore be created once, outside run_one?

bugs.title: Transient handler shadows RateLimited
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_rate_limit_honours_retry_after: legal/1's wait is [['legal/1', 'retry', 0.05]] instead of 0.12. It still makes 2 creates and succeeds.
bugs.why: RateLimited subclasses TransientError, and except clauses are tried top to bottom. With the parent first, a 429 is handled as a plain transient error and the server's 120 ms request is replaced by the 50 ms backoff. The RateLimited clause can never run.
hints: legal/1 is retried, but how long does it wait compared with what the server asked for?
Look at the class hierarchy in errors.py and the order of the except clauses in retry.py.
probes: Why does the retry still succeed, just with the wrong delay?
How could a real server punish a client that ignores Retry-After?

bugs.title: max_attempts excludes the first try
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_transient_errors_retried: '2 != 3' create requests for product. product/1 then shows up in failures as retries_exhausted and pr-01/pr-02 are missing.
bugs.why: max_retries counts retries, not attempts. With max_retries = 2 the batch needs three create requests, but only two are made, so product/1 gives up after the 500 and the 503.
hints: How many create requests did product make, and what did the last one return?
Follow where create_with_retries gets its number of attempts.
probes: Why does legal/1 still succeed with this slip?
Where does the product failure show up besides this test?

bugs.title: Poll pause never awaited
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_polls_wait_between_checks: no poll waits recorded for news/1 ([] instead of three 0.01 waits), although it was still polled 4 times. A 'coroutine ... was never awaited' RuntimeWarning is printed.
bugs.why: Calling an async function without await only creates a coroutine object; its body (recording the wait and sleeping) never runs. The client then polls back to back. Python's 'coroutine was never awaited' RuntimeWarning is the tell.
hints: news/1 was polled four times, yet no poll waits were recorded. Any warnings in the output?
Look at how the poll loop pauses between checks.
probes: Why did the job still complete correctly?
What would this do to a real API's rate limit?

bugs.title: Failed batches dropped after gather
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_failed_batch_reported: failures.get('support/1') is None instead of 'input_too_long'. failures is empty.
bugs.why: With return_exceptions=True, gather hands exceptions back as values. Only the successes are used, so support/1's JobFailed disappears: its documents are missing and nothing says why.
hints: The support documents aren't embedded, but failures is empty. Where did the exception go?
Look at what happens to each gather outcome in run_batches.
probes: What would happen without return_exceptions=True if one batch failed?
Why is silently dropping a failed batch worse than crashing?

bugs.title: Next page read from the echoed token
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_faq_embeddings: faq-06 is missing from the FAQ norms; the other six match.
bugs.why: The server echoes the token that was sent as `page_token` (null on the first page) and puts the next one in `next_page_token`. Reading the echo stops after page one, so faq/1 (6 docs, page size 5) loses faq-06.
hints: Only one FAQ document is missing. Which batch is it in, and how many results pages does that batch have?
Look at which field the results loop takes the next token from.
probes: Why are all the other batches complete?
What data change would have exposed this in more than one batch?

context_qa.a: It loads config, collections and documents, builds the batches with `make_batches`, creates a `BatchClient`, runs `runner.run_batches` with `asyncio.run`, then turns the embeddings into dims/norm and returns batches, embedded, failures, skipped and the client's `waits` list.

context_qa.q: What does run_one do for a single batch?
context_qa.a: Inside an `async with` block it calls `create_with_retries`, then `client.wait_until_done`, then `client.results`, and returns a dict of doc id → embedding vector.

context_qa.q: How are errors classified from an HTTP response?
context_qa.a: `errors.raise_for_status` raises `RateLimited` (with `retry_after_seconds`) for 429, `TransientError` for 500/502/503/504, and `ApiError` for any other status >= 400. RateLimited is a subclass of TransientError, which is a subclass of ApiError.

context_qa.q: How does the mock server behave for each collection?
context_qa.a: legal's first create returns 429 with `retry_after_ms: 120`; product's first two creates return 500 and 503; news jobs need 4 polls before completing; any job with an input over 120 characters finishes as `failed` with code `input_too_long`. Results pages include `page_token` (the token sent) and `next_page_token`.
It appends `[label, kind, round(seconds, 3)]` to `self.waits` and then awaits the injected `sleep` function. Tests inject a sleep that returns immediately.

context_qa.q: Where does the number of create attempts come from?
context_qa.a: `create_with_retries` loops `range(client.config.max_attempts)`; `max_attempts` is a property on `Config` in config.py. It pauses between attempts but not after the last one, then raises `ApiError('retries_exhausted')`.

context_qa.q: How does the server measure concurrency?
context_qa.a: Every request increments an in-flight counter on arrival and decrements it after replying (each request takes about 20 ms). `max_inflight` is the peak value.
